topic.subject: science
topic.title: Body movements
topic.scope: skeleton, joints, muscles, cartilage, movement in animals such as earthworm, snail, fish, birds

misconceptions.statement: Muscles can push bones to move them.
misconceptions.why: Students often equate muscular effort with pushing an object away from themselves.
misconceptions.fix: Muscles can only pull by contracting; they cannot push. Movement occurs because pairs of muscles work together, where one pulls while the other relaxes.

probe.question: How does your arm move when you straighten your elbow?
probe.wrong_answer: The muscle on the front of the arm pushes the bone to make it straight.

misconceptions.statement: Muscles are only present in the arms and legs.
misconceptions.why: Students focus on visible movement and ignore internal organs or the torso.
misconceptions.fix: Muscles are attached to bones throughout the body, including the chest, back, and neck, to support posture and movement.

probe.question: Do we have muscles in our neck and back?
probe.wrong_answer: No, muscles are only found where we can see them bulge, like in our arms.

misconceptions.statement: All joints in the body allow for movement.
misconceptions.why: The word 'joint' is colloquially associated with flexible hinges or connections.
misconceptions.fix: Some joints, like those in the skull, are fixed and do not allow any movement between the bones.

probe.question: Can you move the bones of your skull?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because all bones are connected by joints, and joints are meant for moving.

misconceptions.statement: Bones are solid, hard structures that cannot bend at all.
misconceptions.why: Students perceive bones as rigid, rock-like objects based on skeletal models.
misconceptions.fix: Cartilage is a flexible, bone-like tissue found at joints that allows for smooth movement and slight bending.

probe.question: How can our ears bend if they are made of bone?
probe.wrong_answer: The ear is not made of bone, it is made of skin because bones are too hard to bend.

misconceptions.statement: Earthworms move by using legs that are too small to see.
misconceptions.why: Students assume all animals must have legs to move, based on their experience with vertebrates.
misconceptions.fix: Earthworms move by extending and contracting their body segments using tiny bristles called setae to grip the ground.

probe.question: How does an earthworm crawl without legs?
probe.wrong_answer: It has very tiny legs hidden under its skin that help it walk.

misconceptions.statement: Fish swim by moving their fins like oars.
misconceptions.why: Students compare fish movement to human rowing or swimming techniques.
misconceptions.fix: Fish swim primarily by creating waves with their body and tail, while fins are mainly used for balance and steering.

probe.question: What part of the fish's body provides the main force for swimming?
probe.wrong_answer: The fins, because they act like paddles to push the water back.

requires_topics: Basic parts of the human body
